facts.claim: Issue #26469 exists in pola-rs/polars, titled 'Polars-1.38: LazyFrame becomes slow', and reports slowdowns on 1.38.0 and 1.38.1 versus 1.37.1

The issue's diagnosed causes are set_engine_affinity now affecting collect_all, CSPE not applying to the streaming engine under collect_all, and the streaming engine refusing to run two or more memory-intensive sinks at once. The seed's framing (plan construction or query optimisation of wide or deep lazy queries) is not what the issue diagnoses

The issue was closed as completed on Feb 10, 2026 by a commit linked to PR #26501, which resolved the streaming sink-concurrency cause; the CSPE cause was moved to issue #26502 and is not addressed by that PR
The repository is licensed under the MIT License (copyright Ritchie Vink, and NVIDIA for some portions)

Python Polars release py-2.0.0 exists (dated 06 Oct) and its notes list a performance fix for plan-time regressions in projection pushdown on wide frames (#28724), a later public fix relevant to wide-query planning
The measured speedup of the upstream fix on the seed's shapes

spike_plan.kill_if: No shape family shows a stable slowdown at the pinned parent, or the build exceeds about 3 hours or 16 GB (then K7 or K12-scale cost).
spike_plan.pass_if: Parent is at least 1.5x slower than the fix on at least two shape families, outputs match, and the wheel builds in under 2 hours with under 16 GB RAM.
steps: Before any build, reconcile the pin: the issue's diagnosed cause is streaming and collect_all scheduling, not plan construction. Find the commit where wide-frame plan-time slowdown exists (parent of #28724) and confirm which one the task targets.

In a networked throwaway container, check out the parent of PR #26501 and the parent of #28724, and build the Python wheel with maturin, timing the build and peak RAM (cap at 16 GB). Record the build time; smoke_build was not run.
Write a 20-line generator of wide (500+ columns) and deep (many chained with_columns, when/then nesting) lazy queries; time build-plus-explain() and collect() for each shape at both commits.
Check that the parent commit is measurably slower than the fixed commit on at least two shape families, and that outputs and explain() strings are identical after the fix.
Run three repeats to check determinism of wall-clock medians and record the speedup of the upstream fix over the parent as the reference.

v1.summary: Polars is a real MIT-licensed repo, and issue #26469 and its fix PR #26501 exist, but the issue's diagnosed cause is streaming/collect_all scheduling rather than the wide/deep plan construction the seed describes, so the pin and target must be reconciled (the wide-frame planning fix is #28724 in py-2.0.0). The fixes are public, so the snapshot must be history-less, and build cost is unknown because smoke_build was not run; the spike must confirm the target and build time before the card is trusted.

v2.note: Issue #26469, the fix PR #26501 and the MIT licence are confirmed. The fetched issue contradicts the seed's framing: the regression is streaming-engine sink concurrency and collect_all/engine-affinity scheduling, not plan construction for wide or deep queries. The actual fix is one lever (the sink concurrency limit), and the CSPE part was split off to #26502. Wall-clock timing of concurrent sinks is noisy. The reference speedup has not been measured. Full Polars Rust rebuilds in 16 GB under gVisor make every iteration slow, and the build is unsmoked. The plan-equality gate would reject valid fixes that change the plan shape. A possible rescue would be re-pinning to the parent of #28724 (plan-time slowdown in projection pushdown on wide frames) and measuring several shape families, but as written the seed is one-lever and mis-pinned.
